subject: Elmbridge RFI: privileged access, key custody, and cross-border export controls
messages:
From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@elmbridge.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@elmbridge.com
Date: 2026-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Elmbridge RFI: privileged access and cross-border controls

Diego,

Thanks for agreeing to take our RFI. Attached is our standard export-controls worksheet and a short set of follow-up questions the compliance team raised during the vendor shortlist. High level asks:

- Please confirm key custody model(s) available for hosted and private deployments (BYOK, Redwood KMS, HSM options).
- Describe privileged access controls for support and engineering (break-glass, just-in-time, approval workflow, audit retention).
- For customers storing EU personal data, describe cross-border routing fallbacks and whether processing is ever routed outside EU for failover.
- Provide evidence artifacts (architecture diagram, ACL matrix, sample audit log record).

We would like concise answers and any attachments you can share. If you prefer a short call to walk through, happy to schedule next week.

Regards,
Sofia Ramirez
Head of Vendor Assurance | Elmbridge Therapeutics
security@elmbridge.com

Attachment: elmbridge_rfi_template.xlsx (Excel worksheet - questions)

Subject: Re: Elmbridge RFI: privileged access and cross-border controls

Sofia,

Appreciate the RFI and clear asks — see responses below and attached artifacts. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk through anything. Proposed times: Tue/Wed next week (US morning / EU afternoon).

Summary answers (short):
- Key custody: We support three models: Redwood-managed KMS (default, multi-tenant HSM-backed), customer BYOK via Cloud KMS (customers provide keys in their cloud project), and an enterprise HSM integration for Private (on-prem / VPC) deployments where keys never leave customer boundary.
- Privileged access: Support/eng access is JIT via our access broker (time-limited session tokens), requires 2-person approval for break-glass, session recording and immutable audit logs retained per contract (default 90 days, extendable). Emergent access is logged and reviewed within 24 hours.
- Cross-border routing: For EU-controlled data we offer region-restricted deployments and routing policies that pin processing to EU regions. Our failover policy first attempts EU-zone replica in the same region; as a last-resort fallback we will not route live processing to non-EU without prior contract amendment. Where customers require absolute guarantees, Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) is recommended.

Attachments included: redwood_privileged_access_matrix.pdf, kmscustody_diagram.png, export_controls_summary.docx.

If you need a redacted sample audit log line or a minimal network diagram excerpt, I can include that in a follow-up.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Security Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

Diego/Karthik —

Draft language and deliverables below that I recommend we send to Elmbridge. I've kept the answers concise and evidence-focused:

1) Key custody (brief):
- Redwood-managed keys: HSM-backed, FIPS 140-2 validated HSMs at our cloud provider; keys stored per-customer namespace.
- BYOK: customers can bring keys to their cloud KMS; we never store plaintext keys.
- Private/HSM: for Private customers we provide an integration pattern where keys are provisioned and managed within the customer's HSM or KMIP-enabled appliance; we will include a sample runbook for key rotation and emergency rollover.

Evidence artifacts to include: redwood_privileged_access_matrix.pdf (matrix mapping roles to capabilities), kmscustody_diagram.png (key flow for BYOK and Private), export_controls_summary.docx (bullet summary), and a redacted sample audit log (1-line CSV).

2) Privileged access (brief):
- JIT access broker with approval workflow (two approvers for break-glass), ephemeral VPN session tokens, session capture.
- Audit retention configurable contractually; default 90 days, archive options to 24 months.
- SIEM: we support forwarding audit events to customer SIEM via TLS syslog or API (please indicate preferred endpoint).

3) Cross-border processing/failover (brief):
- Data residency control: we offer region pinning; for EU data processing we recommend Dedicated or Private if customer requires technical guarantees.
- Failover: primary->regional-replica->same-region-failover. We will not redirect processing to non-EU regions without documented agreement.

Next steps: I'll assemble the one-page Private key custody excerpt and a redacted audit sample. Diego, please approve the draft below and I will attach the four artifacts.

Marissa
Senior Product Security Manager
Redwood Inference

Sofia —

Thanks for the patience. Per the RFI attached is a consolidated response and supporting artifacts. Summary and attachments below. If you prefer a 30-min walkthrough we can schedule for Tue/Wed next week.

Consolidated summary (high level):
- Key custody: Redwood-managed KMS (HSM-backed), BYOK via customer cloud KMS, and Private HSM integration. See kmscustody_diagram.png for key flows and export_controls_summary.docx for contractual options.
- Privileged access: JIT broker, two-person approval for break-glass, session recording, configurable audit retention (default 90 days). We support SIEM forwarding — please provide your ingest endpoint and preferred format.
- Cross-border: For EU personal data we use region pinning. Failover attempts remain within EU first; routing to non-EU occurs only under explicit contractual amendment. Private deployment provides the contractual and technical guarantee against cross-border processing.

Attached artifacts: redwood_privileged_access_matrix.pdf, kmscustody_diagram.png, export_controls_summary.docx, elmbridge_rfi_template_filled.xlsx (our answers populated). Also included: redacted_audit_sample.csv (one-line sample).

Also indicate whether you require a Private deployment proposal and we will route to Sales for a dedicated sizing and pricing doc.
